meta.what_this_is: One row per page on the site. Each row states the strongest thing the page asserts, what a reader has to click to check it, and whether this session was able to check it. It is a cross-artefact audit: the site checked against itself, page by page.
meta.why_it_exists: Every other register on this site is organised by topic — flags, questions, sources. None of them answers the question a reviewer actually asks: 'this page says a thing; is it true?' That needs a row per page.

verdicts.holds: This session opened the source and the claim is supported by it.
verdicts.holds-with-caveat: Supported, but only in a narrower form than the page's wording suggests.
verdicts.unverifiable-here: The claim may be true, but checking it needs access this repository does not have.
verdicts.should-be-removed-or-reworded: The claim, as written, is not supported by anything this session could open.

meta.method: Every row was produced by opening the generated page, reading its strongest assertion, then opening the cited source. Where no source is cited, that is recorded as the finding.

rows.claim: Each of the five picks was 'opened, followed to the Amazon listing it lands on, and matched to the product named here'.
rows.check: Open each submitted link and compare the landing title with the name on the card.
rows.checked: Yes — all five opened this session.
rows.note: All five destinations agree with the register. Matching a destination is not the same as matching the owner's intent; that is FLG-001.

rows.claim: As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.
rows.check: Compare the sentence with the Operating Agreement, and compare the placement rule with the FTC guidance.
rows.note: The sentence is verbatim and required. Since the merge with main the site publishes no synthetic tag, so the disclosure and the link state agree: the relationship is declared as an obligation, not claimed as a credited fact. Attribution is unproven until a click appears in an Associates report (FLG-002).

rows.claim: Ratings, prices and stock are 'left where they belong: on Amazon, changing in real time'.
rows.check: Search the page source for a price, a rating or a stock word.
rows.checked: Yes — the build gate rejects any of these strings.
rows.note: Consistent with Program Policies 2(b), which permits a price only from an Amazon-served link or the APIs.

rows.claim: The seasonal band is headed by a photograph of a kitchen counter.
rows.check: Open the asset and compare it with images.json's stated rule, then check the whole set.
rows.checked: Yes — every image referenced by the live pages was opened this session.
rows.note: Corrected during this session. My first pass found one photoreal image here and called it an outlier. Opening the rest showed eight of seventeen in-use images were photographic, including P-02, P-04, the thermometer guide and the cleanup guide — so the register's stated rule ('illustrative editorial photography only') described almost nothing. All eight have been replaced with engravings and the rule now describes the set.

rows.claim: Capacities and features are stated 'in the seller's wording'.
rows.check: Open the listing and compare the title text with the quoted phrases.
rows.checked: Yes — titles transcribed this session for all five.
rows.note: The quoted capacities (6 qt / two 3 qt, 8 qt, 26 qt) all appear in the listing titles.

rows.claim: Adding to basket opens the reader's Amazon cart, with no affiliate tag attached.
rows.check: Open the add.html endpoint and see what Amazon returns.
rows.checked: Yes — Amazon returned a sign-in page with an Associates return path.
rows.note: The endpoint accepts the URL and, for an anonymous visitor, returns a sign-in page first. The permalink carries no AssociateTag, matching the withdrawn-tag state, so the click is a plain reference link and the button does not pretend otherwise.

rows.claim: '7 min read', '5 min read' and so on.
rows.check: Extract the main text and divide the word count by a plausible reading speed.
rows.checked: Yes — one guide measured at about 800 words in the main text.
rows.note: 800 words is roughly 3–4 minutes at 200–250 wpm, not 7. The labels are a self-estimate, not a measurement, and they are generous to the site. Recorded as a wording issue, not a factual claim about a product.

rows.claim: Formats and stated capacities can be compared across all five products.
rows.check: Each cell against the listing title.
rows.note: No cell states a price, a rating or an availability. The table compares form factor only.

rows.claim: Answers recommend a format, not a specific product.
rows.check: Walk the questions and look at the output.
rows.checked: Yes — the output names a format.
rows.note: Important distinction: a recommender that named a product would be making an unverified performance claim. This one does not.

rows.claim: Every factual cell carries a source.
rows.checked: Partly — the Amazon and FTC sources opened; two carry caveats recorded on this page.
rows.note: One FTC URL used elsewhere in the repository (consumer.ftc.gov/business-guidance) is a redirect target, not the canonical page. The canonical page opened is the one linked here.

rows.claim: 22 items where the site is less certain than it would like.
rows.check: Count the rows and read the severities.
rows.note: Self-consistent. Two new findings from this session are added rather than folded into existing flags, so the count on this page and the count on /verification/ differ by design.

rows.claim: 10 of 22 questions are 'closed with a source or a reproducible check'.
rows.check: Open the answer card behind each closed row.
rows.note: The closed rows rest on policy text, which opened. But the two questions that matter most for revenue (Q-01, Q-03) are both open, so the 'closed' count is not a measure of readiness.

rows.claim: The ranking is arithmetic from stated weights.
rows.checked: Yes — the page and the terminal use the same function.
rows.note: The weights are judgements. They were changed once during this session, after the first run ranked a tidying task above the task that decides whether any money can arrive; the change is recorded in offers.json rather than applied silently.

rows.claim: Each section's strongest claim has been checked against a source.
rows.checked: Yes — this is the record of doing it.
rows.note: The audit covers the pages this session could open. It is not a guarantee that no weaker claim elsewhere is wrong; it covers the strongest claim on each of the main surfaces.

rows.claim: The sitemap lists every canonical page and nothing else.
rows.check: Compare the URL count with the build's GENERATED set.
rows.checked: Yes — 29 URLs against 30 generated pages minus 404.
rows.note: The retired editions under archive/ are absent from the sitemap, which is correct, but 22 of them carry no noindex tag and are live on the host. See the deploy-scope row on /verification/.

rows.check: Fetch the host and see what actually resolves.
rows.note: Allow: / is accurate about the host and wrong about the intent: it invites a crawler into /tools/, /src/, /archive/ and five retired storefronts, because the host serves the whole repository. The directive is not the bug; the deploy scope is.
